t2.descripcion:
The passive reflexive is very common in Spanish. It is formed with SE + verb in the third person (singular or plural, depending on the subject) and is used to express actions without mentioning the agent. The subject is the element that receives the action.
• The verb agrees with the subject: Se venden pisos (plural) / Se vende piso (singular).
• It does not take an explicit agent: *Se venden pisos por la inmobiliaria (incorrect).
• It is equivalent to the passive with ser, but it is more frequent in spoken language: Se arreglan bicicletas = Bicicletas son arregladas.
• It is used on signs, advertisements and in everyday language: Aquí se habla español.
• It can take complements: Se entregaron los premios a los ganadores.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The passive reflexive only admits thing subjects, not person subjects. For people, the impersonal with se is used.
❌ COMMON MISTAKE: Using the verb in the singular when the subject is plural: *Se vende pisos (incorrect). It should be: Se venden pisos.
ejemplos: Se entregaron los premios a los ganadores.

t1.descripcion:
The passive voice is used to highlight the action or the result, not the agent. It is formed with the verb SER conjugated + past participle (which agrees in gender and number with the patient subject) + por + agent (optional).
• The patient subject is the one that receives the action: La casa fue construida por los romanos.
• The participle agrees with the subject: Las cartas fueron escritas por Juan.
• The agent is introduced with 'por'; if it is a thing, sometimes with 'de': El libro fue escrito por Cervantes.
• It is used more in written language (news, reports, academic texts): El acuerdo fue firmado ayer.
• The tense of SER indicates the time of the action: La noticia será publicada mañana.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: In Spanish, the passive voice with ser is less frequent than in English or Chinese; the active or the passive reflexive is often preferred.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Forgetting the agreement of the participle: *Las cartas fueron escrito (incorrect). It should be: Las cartas fueron escritas.
ejemplos: La casa fue construida por los romanos.
Las cartas fueron escritas por Juan.
El libro fue escrito por Cervantes.

t3.descripcion:
The impersonal se is used to express actions without a specific subject, generalizing. It is conjugated in the third person singular. It has no lexical subject; the se is the marker of impersonality.
• It is used to talk about general actions or to give instructions: Se dice que va a llover.
• It can be used with transitive and intransitive verbs: Se vive bien aquí.
• With transitive verbs, the direct object can be a person and, then, it takes the preposition 'a': Se vio a los ladrones.
• It is equivalent to 'uno' or 'la gente': Se trabaja mucho en esta empresa.
• It is used in recipes, instructions and rules: Se calienta el agua y se añade el arroz.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: Do not confuse with the passive reflexive: in the impersonal, the verb is always in the singular and the direct object (if there is one) does not agree with the verb.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Making the verb agree with the direct object in the impersonal: *Se vieron a los ladrones (incorrect in impersonal; correct in passive reflexive with a thing subject). It should be: Se vio a los ladrones.
ejemplos: Se dice que va a llover.
Se trabaja mucho en esta empresa.
Se calienta el agua y se añade el arroz.

t4.descripcion:
In this section we contrast the three structures and look at advanced uses in texts and formal contexts.
• Passive with ser: emphasizes the process or the result, with an explicit agent. E.g.: La ley fue aprobada por el parlamento.
• Passive refleja: emphasizes the action without an agent, with a thing as subject. E.g.: Se aprobó la ley.
• Impersonal with se: there is no subject, general action. E.g.: Se aprobó a los candidatos.
• In Spanish, the passive with ser is more frequent in formal and written registers; in spoken language the other two are preferred.
• With verbs like 'decir', 'creer', 'pensar', the impersonal se is used to attribute general opinions: Se cree que habrá elecciones.
📌 IMPORTANT NOTE: The passive with ser can take an agent complement; the passive refleja and the impersonal, cannot. If you need to mention the agent, use the passive with ser or the active voice.
❌ COMMON ERROR: Using 'se' with a plural person subject in passive refleja: *Se vieron a los alumnos (incorrect). For people, use the impersonal: Se vio a los alumnos.
ejemplos: La ley fue aprobada por el parlamento.
Se vieron las estrellas desde el telescopio.
